NKJV.1: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
NKJV.2: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
NKJV.3: What profit has a man from all his labor In which he toils under the sun?
NKJV.4: One generation passes away, and another generation comes; But the earth abides forever.
NKJV.5: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, And hastens to the place where it arose.
NKJV.6: The wind goes toward the south, And turns around to the north; The wind whirls about continually, And comes again on its circuit.
NKJV.7: All the rivers run into the sea, Yet the sea is not full; To the place from which the rivers come, There they return again.
NKJV.8: All things are full of labor; Man cannot express it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor the ear filled with hearing.
NKJV.9: That which has been is what will be, That which is done is what will be done, And there is nothing new under the sun.
NKJV.10: Is there anything of which it may be said, “See, this is new”? It has already been in ancient times before us.
NKJV.11: There is no remembrance of former things, Nor will there be any remembrance of things that are to come By those who will come after.
NKJV.12: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
NKJV.13: And I set my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven; this burdensome task God has given to the sons of man, by which they may be exercised.
NKJV.14: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and indeed, all is vanity and grasping for the wind.
NKJV.15: What is crooked cannot be made straight, And what is lacking cannot be numbered.
NKJV.16: I communed with my heart, saying, “Look, I have attained greatness, and have gained more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My heart has understood great wisdom and knowledge.”
NKJV.17: And I set my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is grasping for the wind.
NKJV.18: For in much wisdom is much grief, And he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.

ESV.1: The words of the Preacher,  the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
ESV.2: Vanity  of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities! All is vanity.
ESV.3: What does man gain by all the toil at which he toils under the sun?
ESV.4: A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth remains forever.
ESV.5: The sun rises, and the sun goes down, and hastens  to the place where it rises.
ESV.6: The wind blows to the south and goes around to the north; around and around goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns.
ESV.7: All streams run to the sea, but the sea is not full; to the place where the streams flow, there they flow again.
ESV.8: All things are full of weariness; a man cannot utter it; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
ESV.9: What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done, and there is nothing new under the sun.
ESV.10: Is there a thing of which it is said, “See, this is new”? It has been already in the ages before us.
ESV.11: There is no remembrance of former things,  nor will there be any remembrance of later things  yet to be among those who come after.
ESV.12: I the Preacher have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
ESV.13: And I applied my heart  to seek and to search out by wisdom all that is done under heaven. It is an unhappy business that God has given to the children of man to be busy with.
ESV.14: I have seen everything that is done under the sun, and behold, all is vanity  and a striving after wind.
ESV.15: What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
ESV.16: I said in my heart, “I have acquired great wisdom, surpassing all who were over Jerusalem before me, and my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
ESV.17: And I applied my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is but a striving after wind.
ESV.18: For in much wisdom is much vexation, and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.

NASB.1: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
NASB.2: 'Vanity of vanities,' says the Preacher, 'Vanity of vanities! All is vanity.'
NASB.3: What advantage does man have in all his work Which he does under the sun?
NASB.4: A generation goes and a generation comes, But the earth remains forever.
NASB.5: Also, the sun rises and the sun sets; And hastening to its place it rises there [again].
NASB.6: Blowing toward the south, Then turning toward the north, The wind continues swirling along; And on its circular courses the wind returns.
NASB.7: All the rivers flow into the sea, Yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, There they flow again.
NASB.8: All things are wearisome; Man is not able to tell [it]. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor is the ear filled with hearing.
NASB.9: That which has been is that which will be, And that which has been done is that which will be done. So there is nothing new under the sun.
NASB.10: Is there anything of which one might say, 'See this, it is new '? Already it has existed for ages Which were before us.
NASB.11: There is no remembrance of earlier things; And also of the later things which will occur, There will be for them no remembrance Among those who will come later [still].
NASB.12: I, the Preacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
NASB.13: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom concerning all that has been done under heaven. [It] is a grievous task [which] God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
NASB.14: I have seen all the works which have been done under the sun, and behold, all is vanity and striving after wind.
NASB.15: What is crooked cannot be straightened and what is lacking cannot be counted.
NASB.16: I said to myself, 'Behold, I have magnified and increased wisdom more than all who were over Jerusalem before me; and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.'
NASB.17: And I set my mind to know wisdom and to know madness and folly; I realized that this also is striving after wind.
NASB.18: Because in much wisdom there is much grief, and increasing knowledge [results in] increasing pain.

NLT.1: These are the words of the Teacher, King David’s son, who ruled in Jerusalem.
NLT.2: “Everything is meaningless,” says the Teacher, “completely meaningless!”
NLT.3: What do people get for all their hard work under the sun?
NLT.4: Generations come and generations go, but the earth never changes.
NLT.5: The sun rises and the sun sets, then hurries around to rise again.
NLT.6: The wind blows south, and then turns north. Around and around it goes, blowing in circles.
NLT.7: Rivers run into the sea, but the sea is never full. Then the water returns again to the rivers and flows out again to the sea.
NLT.8: Everything is wearisome beyond description. No matter how much we see, we are never satisfied. No matter how much we hear, we are not content.
NLT.9: History merely repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new.
NLT.10: Sometimes people say, “Here is something new!” But actually it is old; nothing is ever truly new.
NLT.11: We don’t remember what happened in the past, and in future generations, no one will remember what we are doing now.
NLT.12: I, the Teacher, was king of Israel, and I lived in Jerusalem.
NLT.13: I devoted myself to search for understanding and to explore by wisdom everything being done under heaven. I soon discovered that God has dealt a tragic existence to the human race.
NLT.14: I observed everything going on under the sun, and really, it is all meaningless — like chasing the wind.
NLT.15:
What is wrong cannot be made right.
What is missing cannot be recovered.
NLT.16: I said to myself, “Look, I am wiser than any of the kings who ruled in Jerusalem before me. I have greater wisdom and knowledge than any of them.”
NLT.17: So I set out to learn everything from wisdom to madness and folly. But I learned firsthand that pursuing all this is like chasing the wind.
NLT.18:
The greater my wisdom, the greater my grief.
To increase knowledge only increases sorrow.

AMP.1: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
AMP.2:
"Vanity of vanities," says the Preacher.
"Vanity of vanities! All [that is done without God's guidance] is vanity [futile, meaningless—a wisp of smoke, a vapor that vanishes, merely chasing the wind]."
AMP.3:
What advantage does man have from all his work
Which he does under the sun (while earthbound)?
AMP.4:
One generation goes and another generation comes,
But the earth remains forever.
AMP.5:
Also, the sun rises and the sun sets;
And hurries to the place where it rises again.
AMP.6:
The wind blows toward the south,
Then circles toward the north;
The wind circles and swirls endlessly,
And on its circular course the wind returns.
AMP.7:
All the rivers flow into the sea,
Yet the sea is not full.
To the place where the rivers flow,
There they flow again.
AMP.8:
All things are wearisome and all words are frail;
Man cannot express it.
The eye is not satisfied with seeing,
Nor is the ear filled with hearing.
AMP.9:
That which has been is that which will be [again],
And that which has been done is that which will be done again.
So there is nothing new under the sun.
AMP.10:
Is there anything of which it can be said,
"See this, it is new"?
It has already existed for [the vast] ages [of time recorded or unrecorded]
Which were before us.
AMP.11:
There is no remembrance of earlier things,
Nor also of the later things that are to come;
There will be for them no remembrance
By generations who will come after them.
AMP.12: I, the Preacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
AMP.13: And I set my mind to seek and explore by [man's] wisdom all [human activity] that has been done under heaven. It is a miserable business and a burdensome task which God has given the sons of men with which to be busy and distressed.
AMP.14: I have seen all the works which have been done under the sun, and behold, all is vanity, a futile grasping and chasing after the wind.
AMP.15: What is crooked cannot be straightened and what is defective and lacking cannot be counted.
AMP.16: I spoke with my heart, saying, "Behold, I have acquired great [human] wisdom and experience, more than all who were over Jerusalem before me; and my mind has observed a wealth of [moral] wisdom and [scientific] knowledge."
AMP.17: And I set my mind to know [practical] wisdom and to discern [the character of] madness and folly [in which men seem to find satisfaction]; I realized that this too is a futile grasping and chasing after the wind.
AMP.18: For in much [human] wisdom there is much displeasure and exasperation; increasing knowledge increases sorrow.

MSG.1: These are the words of the Quester, David's son and king in Jerusalem:
MSG.2:
Smoke, nothing but smoke.
That's what the Quester says.]
There's nothing to anything—it's all smoke.
MSG.3:
What's there to show for a lifetime of work,
a lifetime of working your fingers to the bone?
MSG.4:
One generation goes its way, the next one arrives,
but nothing changes—it's business as usual for old
planet earth.
MSG.5:
The sun comes up and the sun goes down,
then does it again, and again—the same old round.
MSG.6:
The wind blows south, the wind blows north.
Around and around and around it blows,
blowing this way, then that—the whirling, erratic wind.
MSG.7:
All the rivers flow into the sea,
but the sea never fills up.
The rivers keep flowing to the same old place,
and then start all over and do it again.
MSG.8:
Everything's boring, utterly boring—
no one can find any meaning in it.
Boring to the eye,
boring to the ear.
MSG.9:
What was will be again,
what happened will happen again.
There's nothing new on this earth.
Year after year it's the same old thing.
MSG.10:
Does someone call out, "Hey, this is new"?
Don't get excited—it's the same old story.
MSG.11:
Nobody remembers what happened yesterday.
And the things that will happen tomorrow?
Nobody'll remember them either.
Don't count on being remembered.
MSG.12: Call me "the Quester." I've been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
MSG.13: I looked most carefully into everything, searched out all that is done on this earth. And let me tell you, there's not much to write home about. God hasn't made it easy for us.
MSG.14: I've seen it all and it's nothing but smoke—smoke, and spitting into the wind.
MSG.15:
Life's a corkscrew that can't be straightened,
A minus that won't add up.
MSG.16: I said to myself, "I know more and I'm wiser than anyone before me in Jerusalem. I've stockpiled wisdom and knowledge."
MSG.17: What I've finally concluded is that so-called wisdom and knowledge are mindless and witless—nothing but spitting into the wind.
MSG.18:
Much learning earns you much trouble.
The more you know, the more you hurt.

NET.4: A generation comes and a generation goes, but the earth remains the same through the ages.
NET.5: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries away to a place from which it rises again.
NET.6: The wind goes to the south and circles around to the north; round and round the wind goes and on its rounds it returns.
NET.7: All the streams flow into the sea, but the sea is not full, and to the place where the streams flow, there they will flow again.
NET.8: All this monotony is tiresome; no one can bear to describe it: The eye is never satisfied with seeing, nor is the ear ever content with hearing.
NET.9: What exists now is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done; there is nothing truly new on earth.
NET.10: Is there anything about which someone can say, “Look at this! It is new!”? It was already done long ago, before our time.
NET.11: No one remembers the former events, nor will anyone remember the events that are yet to happen; they will not be remembered by the future generations.
NET.12: I, the Teacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
NET.13: I decided to carefully and thoroughly examine all that has been accomplished on earth. I concluded: God has given people a burdensome task that keeps them occupied.
NET.14: I reflected on everything that is accomplished by man on earth, and I concluded: Everything he has accomplished is futile — like chasing the wind!
NET.15: What is bent cannot be straightened, and what is missing cannot be supplied.
NET.16: I thought to myself, “I have become much wiser than any of my predecessors who ruled over Jerusalem; I have acquired much wisdom and knowledge.”
NET.17: So I decided to discern the benefit of wisdom and knowledge over foolish behavior and ideas; however, I concluded that even this endeavor is like trying to chase the wind!
NET.18: For with great wisdom comes great frustration; whoever increases his knowledge merely increases his heartache.
